title: The first stall
body: A bookstall opens on the platform at Allahabad, selling newspapers, magazines and books to passengers waiting for their trains.
caption: Allahabad · 1877

title: The Indian Railway Library
body: Wheeler publishes cheap, paper-covered books made for train journeys, including six early collections by Rudyard Kipling, among them Soldiers Three.
caption: Indian Railway Library · 1888–89

title: Along the network
body: As the railway grows, stalls follow it, from great junctions to smaller halts, wherever passengers have time to read.
caption: Date to be confirmed

title: Reading in many languages
body: Newspapers and books in Indian languages take their place beside English titles on the shelves.
caption: Date to be confirmed

title: The Banerjee family
body: Stewardship of the company passes to the Banerjee family, who carry the stalls through a changing country.
caption: Date to be confirmed

title: A new nation, the same platforms
body: Independent India keeps travelling, and keeps reading. The stalls remain a fixture of the station.
caption: Post-Independence

title: Still on the platform
body: Wheeler stalls still serve travellers, and some historic kiosks are now recognised as heritage structures in their own right.
caption: Present day
